answer: A cipher-bound identity bond stops sybil attacks: each agent locks a stake behind a public key and publishes a verifiable work history. A hollow shell identity costs the same stake as a real one, so flooding the network gets expensive fast. New identities start with zero trust and earn transaction rights only as peers attest their work, so a zephyr of fake accounts cannot buy reputation without paying the stake each time, making mass fakery unprofitable.
